glosses: To be moved downwards.

glosses: To be moved downwards.

glosses: To be moved downwards.

glosses: To change, often negatively.

examples.text: Rome fell to the Goths in 410 AD.

glosses: To change, often negatively.
To die, especially in battle or by disease.

examples.text: This is a monument to all those who fell in the First World War.

glosses: To change, often negatively.
To become lower (in quantity, pitch, etc.).

examples.text: The candidate's poll ratings fell abruptly after the banking scandal.

glosses: To occur (on a certain day of the week, date, or similar); to happen.

examples.text: (Thus D-day fell on June 6 rather than the planned June 5.)

glosses: To be allotted to; to arrive through chance, fate, or inheritance.

examples.text: And so it falls to me to make this important decision.

If to her share some female errors fall, / Look on her face, and you'll forget them all.

examples.text: Upon lessening interest to four per cent, you fall the price of your native commodities.

glosses: To issue forth into life; to be brought forth; said of the young of certain animals.

glosses: To descend in character or reputation; to become degraded; to sink into vice, error, or sin.

examples.text: Let us labour therefore to enter into that rest, lest any man fall after the same example of unbelief.

glosses: To become ensnared or entrapped; to be worse off than before.
